extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of aesthetics, artists and writers interested in principles of beauty
extracted.subtask_description: A taxonomy of sensory and formal properties that produce the passion of love (the beautiful) across sight, touch, and hearing, with negative tests (what beauty is not). Useful for writers and artists who wish to evoke 'beauty' in description or design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportion is not the cause of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Proportion and beauty are distinct: proportional measures often occur without beauty, and beauty often exists without the assigned proportions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume mathematically 'correct' proportions will produce beauty. Examples given: proportional measures found in many humans yet not always beautiful; beauty frequently exists without those proportions. Avoid confusing 'proportion' (a cold, intellectual approval) with the passionate response of beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fitness/utility is not the cause of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of an object's fitness or usefulness does not constitute beauty; many structures perfectly adapted to an end are not beautiful to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a pig's snout, pelican's pouch, hedgehog's prickles, elephant's trunk — well-fitted but not beautiful. Fitness and proportion produce approbation by the understanding, not the passionate love proper to beauty. In art, fitness and proportion matter for purpose, but they are distinct from the qualities that elicit beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfection is not the cause of beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Perfection as such does not generate the passion of love; often the highest perfection (especially in the sublime virtues) inspires reverence or terror rather than love.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soft, imperfect, or even signs of weakness (e.g., modesty, blushing, vulnerability) can heighten beauty. Do not equate moral or formal perfection with loveliness in description or character portrayal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beauty is a sensible quality acting mechanically on the mind
rubrics_metrics.description: Beauty primarily depends on positive sensible qualities disposed in bodies that act mechanically upon the human mind via the senses rather than by abstract reason or perceived utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beauty strikes prior to intellectual analysis; it is produced by sensory arrangement. When writing, prioritize immediately perceptible sensory arrangements rather than explanations of use or function to evoke beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smallness (comparative size)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful objects tend to be comparatively small; objects of love are linguistically and affectively treated as diminutives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use small-scale or diminutive imagery to evoke tenderness or love; contrast with the sublime, which dwells on greatness and terror. Examples: little birds, small delicate animals, endearing diminutives in language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: Smooth surfaces are essential to beauty; little or nothing beautiful is rugged or broken in surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A broken or rugged surface usually destroys beauty regardless of other merits. Emphasize polished, flowing, unbroken surfaces in visual or tactile description; avoid sharp projections and abrupt texture changes when aiming for beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual variation (continuous, non-angular lines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of beautiful objects change direction gradually and continuously rather than in straight right lines or abrupt angular shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor 'melted' transitions and continuously varying outlines (the 'line of beauty') over sudden angles. Anti-pattern: angular figures, sudden protuberances, and sharp turns, which produce ugliness. Example imagery: the dove's smoothly changing profile, the insensible swell of neck and breast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delicacy (appearance of fragility)
rubrics_metrics.description: An air of delicacy, even fragility, enhances beauty; robustness and strength are prejudicial to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe fragility, fine texture, and slightness rather than bulk and muscularity when aiming for beauty. Distinguish between unhealthy weakness (which harms other beauty conditions) and delicate charm (which enhances loveliness). Examples: delicate flowers vs. robust forest trees; greyhound vs. mastiff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color qualities for beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: Colors in beautiful bodies should be clean and fair (not dusky or muddy), generally mild rather than strong, and if strong they are diversified and gradated so no single glaring color dominates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use soft, pale, mixed colors (light greens, soft blues, weak whites, pinks, violets) and blend them with gradations rather than stark, saturated, single tones. In complexion, avoid harsh reds or whites; instead show subtle mixes and indeterminate boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union of parts (melting of parts into each other)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parts of beautiful objects should be 'melted' into one another, not distinctly divided by sharp angles or abrupt separations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for seamless transitions among features (forms, colors, textures). Emphasize continuity and integration of parts rather than discrete, mechanically joined elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physiognomy: expression aligned with outer beauty
rubrics_metrics.description: For human beauty, the face (physiognomy) should express gentle and amiable qualities that correspond with the softness, smoothness, and delicacy of the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting beautiful characters, align facial expression and demeanor with the physical qualities—softness and amiability heighten perceived beauty. Avoid discordant interior traits (harshness, sternness) that contradict outward delicacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eye: clearness, slow languid motion, harmonious union
rubrics_metrics.description: The beauty of the eye consists in its clearness (not dull or muddy), a slow/languid motion (more lovely than brisk), and its harmonious union with neighboring features (no strong deviation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe clear, bright eyes with gentle shifting of gaze; avoid dullness, muddiness, rapid darting motion, or eyes that jut oddly from surrounding features. The eye's expressiveness (indicating mind qualities) is a principal source of its beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ugliness as opposite to beauty (distinct from proportion/fitness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ugliness is generally the opposite of the qualities laid down for beauty (roughness, angularity, muddiness, strength), but ugliness is not simply the lack of proportion or fitness and can coexist with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To portray ugliness, emphasize those contrary qualities (sharp angles, coarse texture, muddied color). Remember ugliness can be proportionally ordered or fit for use yet still repulsive in the sense opposed to beauty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace (posture and motion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Gracefulness is closely allied to beauty but specifically belongs to posture and motion: it requires absence of apparent difficulty, slight inflection of the body, composure of parts, roundedness and delicacy of attitude and movement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In describing graceful movement, avoid stiff, effortful, or angular actions. Use smooth, seemingly effortless motion, slight bends and composure of limbs. Examples: classical statues such as the Venus de Medicis or Antinous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elegance and speciousness (regularity and polish)
rubrics_metrics.description: Elegance: composition of smooth, polished parts that do not press on each other and that affect some regular shape; 'specious' or 'fine' applies when such qualities are present at large scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For elegance, emphasize regularity, polish, and harmonious ornamentation (elegant buildings, furniture). If the same qualities are applied at great dimensions, the object becomes 'fine' or 'specious' rather than merely 'beautiful.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful in feeling (touch): slight resistance, softness, and gradual variation
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects pleasant to touch provide slight resistance (smoothness along the surface) and slight pressure-resistance (softness); they also exhibit continual but insensible variation of surface without sudden changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evoking tactile beauty, stress smoothness and softness, gentle warmth, and surfaces that change subtly under the hand. Avoid abrupt textures, angles, and sudden thermal shocks; such changes produce startlement rather than pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beautiful in sounds: softness, smoothness, moderation, and restrained variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Beautiful sounds are soft, delicate, clear, even, smooth and of weak intensity rather than loud, shrill, harsh, or very deep; quick, abrupt variety and rapid transitions are contrary to the genius of the beautiful in music.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To render music or sonic description beautiful, prefer linked, winding, gently prolonged phrases, mellow timbres, and gradual transitions. Avoid loudness, shrillness, excessive contrasts, or hurried shifts that excite mirth or tumult rather than the melting, languid affection of beauty.
